title: Properties of Operations: Commutative, Associative and Distributive
seo_title: Grade 5 Properties of Operations Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Recognise and use the commutative, associative and distributive properties with whole numbers.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 worksheets on properties of operations: commutative, associative and distributive properties. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Order and grouping do not change + and ×.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Commutative: 25 + 48 = 48 + 25 and 6 × 9 = 9 × 6.
  • Associative: (4 × 25) × 7 = 4 × (25 × 7).
  • Distributive: 7 × 46 = 7 × 40 + 7 × 6.
  • These properties work for + and ×, not for − and ÷.

Examples

Example

4 × 37 × 25

(4 × 25) × 37

100 × 37

Answer: 3 700

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
− and ÷ are not commutative12 ÷ 4 ≠ 4 ÷ 12.
One part onlyMultiply both parts.
AddingDistribute the multiplication.

items.e: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 × 8 = 80 is easy. The other groupings with × give the same product, but with harder steps. (2 + 5) × 8 adds instead of multiplying.

items.e: The two parts must add up to 9: 5 + 4 = 9. So the missing number is 4.
The two parts must add up to 8: 3 + 5 = 8. So the missing number is 5.

Split 8 into 5 + 3. Multiply both parts by 7 and add: 35 + 21 = 56. The two parts must add up to 8.
Split 7 into 5 + 2. Multiply both parts by 9 and add: 45 + 18 = 63. The two parts must add up to 7.
Split 6 into 4 + 2. Multiply both parts by 6 and add: 24 + 12 = 36. The two parts must add up to 6.
You can multiply in any order: 7 × 9 = 9 × 7. So ? = 7. Not 63: both sides must be equal, so ? is not the answer to 7 × 9.
Turn-around facts: 12 × 5 = 5 × 12. So ? = 5. Not 60: = means “the same as”, not “the answer is”.
Multiplication can be done in any order, so 5 × 9 = 9 × 5 is true. Division cannot: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 but 4 ÷ 20 is less than 1. 7 × 3 = 21, not 10. 6 × 4 = 24, not 144.

items.q: Work out 5 × 17 × 2. Hint: multiply the 5 and the 2 first.
items.e: Multiply 5 × 2 first: 5 × 2 = 10. Then 10 × 17 = 170. Not 85: that forgets the × 2.

items.q: Work out 4 × 13 × 25. Hint: multiply the 4 and the 25 first.
items.e: Multiply 4 × 25 first: 4 × 25 = 100. Then 100 × 13 = 1 300. Not 325: that forgets the × 4.
2 × 5 = 10, so 2 × 36 × 5 = 36 × 10. ? = 10. Not 7: you multiply 2 and 5, you do not add them.
Split 14 into 10 + 4. 6 × 14 = 6 × 10 + 6 × 4, so ? = 4. Not 14: only the 4 ones are left after the 10.
Split 16 into 10 + 6. 7 × 16 = 7 × 10 + 7 × 6 = 70 + 42, so ? = 42. Not 6: the 6 must be multiplied by 7 too.
Split 23 into 20 + 3. 8 × 23 = 8 × 20 + 8 × 3, so ? = 3. Not 24: that is 8 × 3, but ? is the number that 8 multiplies.
Split 17 into 10 + 7. 5 × 17 = 5 × 10 + 5 × 7 = 50 + 35, so ? = 35. Not 7: the 7 must be multiplied by 5 too.
6 × 18 = 6 × 10 + 6 × 8 = 60 + 48 = 108. Not 68: that is 60 + 8, which forgets to multiply the 8 by 6.
3 × 26 = 3 × 20 + 3 × 6 = 60 + 18 = 78. Not 66: that is 60 + 6, which forgets to multiply the 6 by 3.
19 is 1 less than 20. 9 × 19 = 9 × 20 − 9 × 1 = 180 − 9, so ? = 9. Not 1: take away one group of 9, not just 1. 9 × 19 = 171.

items.e: = means both sides have the same value. The left side is 3 × 8 = 24, so 4 × ? = 24. Use the inverse: ? = 24 ÷ 4 = 6. Not 24: that is the value of the left side, not the missing number.

Which property does this equation show?
4 × 7 = 7 × 4
items.e: This is the commutative property. The factors switch places, and the product stays the same.

items.q:
Which property does this equation show?
(2 × 3) × 4 = 2 × (3 × 4)
items.e: This is the associative property. The factors stay in the same order. Only the parentheses move, which changes what you multiply first.

items.q:
Which property does this equation show?
6 × (5 + 2) = (6 × 5) + (6 × 2)
items.e: This is the distributive property. One factor is split into two parts. Each part is multiplied, and the products are added.

items.q:
Which property does this equation show?
9 × 1 = 9
items.e: This is the identity property of multiplication. Multiplying by 1 keeps the number the same.

items.q:
Which property does this equation show?
0 × 8 = 0
items.e: This is the zero property of multiplication. Multiplying by 0 always gives 0.

items.q:
Which property does this equation show?
(4 × 5) + (4 × 3) = 4 × 8
items.e: This is the distributive property. One factor is split into two parts. Each part is multiplied, and the products are added.

items.q: Which equation shows the commutative property?
items.e: Commutative means the order changes: 3 × 8 and 8 × 3 have the same factors in a different order.

items.q: Which equation shows the distributive property?
items.e: 6 is split into 5 + 1. Each part is multiplied by 7, and the two products are added: 35 + 7 = 42.

items.q: Lerato sets up 6 rows of 8 chairs. Sibusiso sets up 8 rows of 6 chairs. Who sets up more chairs?
items.e: 6 × 8 = 48 and 8 × 6 = 48, so they set up the same number. Switching the order does not change the product. (14 comes from adding 6 + 8.)

items.q: A box has 4 rows of 9 crayons. Lerato says the total is 4 × 9. Ethan says it is 9 × 4. Who is right?
items.e: 4 rows of 9 can also be read as 9 columns of 4. 4 × 9 = 9 × 4 = 36.
